claims.text: Selective PDE-4 inhibitor (more specific than theophylline, fewer adverse effects); anti-inflammatory, only a mild bronchodilator.
claims.quote: Phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4) inhibitors such as roflumilast are more specific than the non-selective phosphodiesterase inhibitor theophylline and have fewer adverse effects. They have anti-inflammatory properties and are mild bronchodilators.
claims.locator: Pharmacotherapy for Stable COPD › Phosphodiesterase inhibitors

claims.text: COPD: add-on for recurrent exacerbations in COPD with chronic bronchitis and FEV1 < 50% (alternative: long-term azithromycin).
claims.quote: For recurrent exacerbations, add either a phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4) inhibitor (eg, roflumilast) or long-term azithromycin. Roflumilast is indicated in patients with COPD (FEV1< 50%) with chronic bronchitis.

claims.text: Not a bronchodilator; not for acute bronchospasm.
claims.quote: DALIRESP is not a bronchodilator and is not indicated for the relief of acute bronchospasm.

claims.text: 500 mcg PO once daily, with or without food; may start 250 mcg daily × 4 weeks to improve tolerance
claims.quote: The maintenance dose for patients with COPD is one 500 mcg tablet per day, with or without food. Starting treatment with a dose of DALIRESP 250 mcg once daily for 4 weeks and increasing to DALIRESP 500 mcg once daily thereafter may reduce the rate of treatment discontinuation in some patients.

claims.text: (250 mcg is not a therapeutic dose).
claims.quote: DALIRESP 250 mcg is a starting dose, for the first 4 weeks of treatment only and is not the effective (therapeutic) dose.

claims.text: Most common: diarrhea, weight loss, nausea, headache, back pain, influenza, insomnia, dizziness, ↓ appetite.
claims.quote: Most common adverse reactions (≥2%) are diarrhea, weight decrease, nausea, headache, back pain, influenza, insomnia, dizziness and decreased appetite.
Treatment with DALIRESP is associated with an increase in psychiatric adverse reactions.

claims.text: Contraindicated in moderate–severe liver impairment (Child-Pugh B or C).
claims.quote: Moderate to severe liver impairment (Child-Pugh B or C) ( 4 )

claims.text: History of depression or suicidality: weigh risks and benefits carefully.
claims.quote: Before using DALIRESP in patients with a history of depression and/or suicidal thoughts or behavior, prescribers should carefully weigh the risks and benefits of treatment with DALIRESP in such patients.

claims.text: Strong CYP inducers (rifampin, phenobarbital, carbamazepine, phenytoin): not recommended
claims.quote: Use with strong cytochrome P450 enzyme inducers (e.g., rifampicin, phenobarbital, carbamazepine, phenytoin) is not recommended.
The administration of the cytochrome P450 enzyme inducer rifampicin resulted in a reduction in exposure, which may result in a decrease in the therapeutic effectiveness of DALIRESP.

claims.text: Monitor weight regularly; evaluate unexplained or significant weight loss and consider stopping.
claims.quote: Monitor weight regularly. If unexplained or clinically significant weight loss occurs, evaluate weight loss and consider discontinuation of DALIRESP.

claims.text: Patient and family should watch for new or worse insomnia, anxiety, depression, suicidal thoughts or mood changes and call the provider if they occur.
claims.quote: Advise patients, their caregivers, and families to be alert for the emergence or worsening of insomnia, anxiety, depression, suicidal thoughts or other mood changes, and if such changes occur to contact their healthcare provider.
